implementation_notes: Foundation supplies the range: DateInterval is a closed interval [start, end] built from two Dates or a start and a duration, with contains(_:), intersects(_:), intersection(with:) and a duration property, so Effectivity holds one interval and asks contains(asOf). Two properties decide the design: DateInterval is closed while Calendar.dateInterval(of:for:) returns half-open calendar units - the Swift forums thread documents that mismatch - and Date is an instant measured in seconds, so date-granularity bounds must be derived from a Calendar (startOfDay(for:), date(byAdding: .day, value: 1, to:)) rather than from second arithmetic. Use the Calendar-based variant when the fact is true for whole calendar days.
pitfalls: DateInterval is closed while Calendar.dateInterval(of:for:) is half-open: taking a day interval from the Calendar and testing DateInterval.contains includes the next day's midnight.
Date is a Double of seconds, so "one day" written as 86 400 seconds is wrong across DST - day arithmetic must go through Calendar.date(byAdding:).
DateComponents and DateInterval bounds are interpreted in a calendar and time zone; a period stored without its zone shifts when read in another one, and Calendar.current changes with user settings.

variants.name: Calendar day-granularity comparison
variants.implementation_notes: When the fact is true for whole calendar days the range can be reduced to its boundaries plus calendar-aware comparisons: store the bounds as DateComponents (or as half-open Calendar-derived Dates) and answer the as-of question with Calendar.compare(_:to:toGranularity: .day), with isDate(_:inSameDayAs:) for day equality. This is DST- and zone-correct because the calendar, not a second count, defines the day, and it keeps "no time of day" out of the model. Choose it when the time of day carries no meaning for the fact and instant containment is never needed; DateInterval remains the right tool when the period has real instant granularity (sessions, leases, timers).
pitfalls: Granularity comparison is calendar- and zone-dependent: the same pair of Dates can compare differently in two zones, so the zone (or the calendar) must be persisted with the period.

DateComponents with only some fields set are completed from the current date (a .day without .year), so incomplete components silently produce today's year - always build complete components or parse with a fixed formatter.
Calendar.current follows the user's region, calendar and zone: domain code must use one explicit Calendar instance, otherwise the same stored period changes meaning per device.
